standards.description: Translate verbal quantitative situations into algebraic expressions and evaluate them for given variable values.

skills.description: Translate between verbal quantitative situations and algebraic expressions, including contextual situations.
Evaluate algebraic expressions that include absolute value, square roots, and cube roots for given replacement values of variables.

standards.description: Perform operations on and factor polynomial expressions in one variable.

skills.description: Determine sums and differences of polynomial expressions in one variable using strategies like concrete objects, pictorial models, and symbolic models.
Determine the product of polynomial expressions in one variable using the distributive property, area models, and concrete/pictorial/symbolic strategies.
Factor completely first- and second-degree polynomials in one variable with integral coefficients, including factoring out the greatest common factor (GCF).
Determine the quotient of polynomials using a monomial, binomial, or completely factored divisor.
Represent and demonstrate equality of quadratic expressions in different forms (concrete, verbal, symbolic, graphical).

standards.description: Derive and apply the laws of exponents to simplify expressions.

skills.description: Derive the laws of exponents through exploration of patterns for products, quotients, and powers of bases.
Simplify multivariable expressions and ratios of monomial expressions with integer exponents using the laws of exponents.

standards.description: Simplify and determine equivalent radical expressions involving square roots and cube roots.

skills.description: Simplify and determine equivalent radical expressions involving the square root of a whole number in simplest form.
Simplify and determine equivalent radical expressions involving the cube root of an integer.
Add, subtract, and multiply radicals limited to numeric square and cube root expressions.
Generate equivalent numerical expressions for radicals using rational exponents (1/2 and 1/3) and justify equivalency.

standards.description: Represent, solve, explain, and interpret solutions to multistep linear equations, inequalities, and literal equations.

skills.description: Write a linear equation or inequality in one variable to represent a contextual situation.
Solve multistep linear equations in one variable, including contextual situations, using properties of real numbers and equality.
Solve multistep linear inequalities in one variable algebraically and graph the solution set on a number line, including contextual situations.
Rearrange a formula or literal equation to solve for a specified variable using properties of equality.
Determine if a linear equation in one variable has one solution, no solution, or an infinite number of solutions.
Verify possible solutions to multistep linear equations and inequalities algebraically, graphically, and with technology.

standards.description: Represent, solve, explain, and interpret solutions to systems of linear equations, inequalities, and linear inequalities in two variables.

skills.description: Create a system of two linear equations in two variables to represent a contextual situation.
Solve a system of two linear equations in two variables algebraically and graphically using properties of real numbers and equality.
Determine whether a system of two linear equations has one solution, no solution, or an infinite number of solutions.
Create a linear inequality in two variables to represent a contextual situation.
Represent the solution of a linear inequality in two variables graphically on a coordinate plane.
Create a system of two linear inequalities in two variables to represent a contextual situation.
Represent the solution set of a system of two linear inequalities in two variables graphically on a coordinate plane.
Verify possible solutions to a system of two linear equations, a linear inequality in two variables, or a system of two linear inequalities algebraically, graphically, and with technology.

standards.description: Represent, solve, and interpret solutions to quadratic equations in one variable.

skills.description: Solve a quadratic equation in one variable over the set of real numbers with rational or irrational solutions, including contextual problems.
Determine and justify if a quadratic equation in one variable has no real solutions, one real solution, or two real solutions.
Verify possible solutions to a quadratic equation in one variable algebraically, graphically, and with technology.

standards.description: Investigate, analyze, and compare linear functions algebraically and graphically, and model linear relationships.

skills.description: Determine and identify the domain, range, zeros, slope, and intercepts of a linear function presented algebraically or graphically.
Investigate and explain how transformations to the parent function y = x affect the rate of change (slope) and the y-intercept of a linear function.
Write equivalent algebraic forms of linear functions, including slope-intercept, standard, and point-slope forms, and analyze the information revealed by each form.
Write the equation of a linear function to model a linear relationship between two quantities, including contextual situations.
Write the equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line through a given point.
Graph a linear function in two variables with and without technology, including contextual situations.
For any value x in the domain of f, determine f(x), and determine x given any value f(x) in the range of f, given an algebraic or graphical representation of a linear function.
Compare and contrast the characteristics of linear functions represented algebraically, graphically, in tables, and in contextual situations.

standards.description: Investigate, analyze, and compare characteristics of functions, including quadratic and exponential functions, and model relationships.

skills.description: Determine whether a relation represented by ordered pairs, tables, mappings, or graphs is a function and, if so, determine the domain and range.
Given an equation or graph, determine key characteristics of a quadratic function including x-intercepts (zeros), y-intercept, vertex, and domain and range.
Graph a quadratic function in two variables using transformations and other strategies.
Make connections between the algebraic (standard and factored forms) and graphical representation of a quadratic function.
Given an equation or graph of an exponential function in the form y = ab^x, interpret key characteristics including y-intercepts and domain and range.
Graph an exponential function in two variables using transformations and other strategies.
For any value x in the domain of f, determine f(x) of a quadratic or exponential function and determine x given any value f(x) in the range of a quadratic function.
Compare and contrast the key characteristics of linear, quadratic, and exponential functions using tables and graphs.

standards.description: Apply the data cycle to represent bivariate data in scatterplots and determine the curve of best fit using linear and quadratic functions.

skills.description: Formulate investigative questions that require the collection or acquisition of bivariate data.
Determine what variables could be used to explain a given contextual problem or situation or answer investigative questions.
Determine an appropriate method to collect a representative sample, which could include a simple random sample, to answer an investigative question.

Given a table of ordered pairs or a scatterplot representing no more than 30 data points, use technology to determine whether a linear or quadratic function represents the relationship and find the equation of the curve of best fit.
Use linear and quadratic regression methods to write a function representing the data and describe the strengths and weaknesses of the model.
Use a linear model to predict outcomes and evaluate the strength and validity of these predictions using technology.
Investigate and explain the meaning of the rate of change (slope) and y-intercept (constant term) of a linear model in context.
Analyze relationships between two quantitative variables revealed in a scatterplot.
Make conclusions based on the analysis of a set of bivariate data and communicate the results.
